review: First text pass. Mechanically relevant profile, knowledge, reaction, time, advancement, mapping and encounter procedures enumerated; linked reaction tables and trait contracts remain pending.

excluded_material.reason: General storytelling, group management, adventure-writing advice, quoted fiction, example plots and online-service discussion have no additional required executable mechanic and are not repository content.
Worldbuilding prose is represented only by explicit required world parameters; no sample setting fiction is copied.

entries.acceptance: Campaign profiles explicitly select optional rules and authored interpretations; a cinematic style or high starting budget alone does not activate every cinematic procedure.
The campaign supplies the actual starting point budget; suggested power bands are descriptive guidance rather than exact legal ranges.

An optional staged budget first approves a character built on base points, then applies remaining points under advancement restrictions; retain both stages without treating the second as unrestricted creation.
A campaign may require a fixed trait/template package and grant a separate discretionary budget; charge the package exactly once and validate its prerequisites.
An optional character policy can reserve minimum point percentages for declared ability categories; explicitly define category membership and overlapping contributions before validating totals.
Campaign-specific caps can restrict individual attributes or total attribute expenditure; defaults must not silently impose caps from a different campaign.
Authored exceptional rulings and stochastic world facts need a stated situation, allowed outcome and committed result. Preserve that decision for replay; no automatic reroll on preview.
Character knowledge is separate from world truth. Player and nonplayer decisions must use their actual observations, languages and learned information, not private records exposed by an assessment.

Important nonplayer characters can use full accounting; incidental characters may have explicitly incomplete profiles. If an incidental statistic is generated with three dice, store it on that character rather than regenerating each use.
A nonpredetermined reaction uses secret three dice plus reaction modifiers, with higher totals favorable; it is not a roll-under check and must not inherit success-roll critical thresholds.

Apply relevant appearance, behavior, social traits and apparent status of the person interacting, with actual audience applicability and bias traits. Do not sum every party member's bonuses indiscriminately.

A successful context-appropriate skill can grant +2 reaction. Skill twenty or more gives automatic +2 for diplomacy or fast-talk when speech is allowed and merchant during trade; additional skill applicability requires author approval.
An authored appropriate approach can grant +1 or more, while an antagonistic approach can impose -1 or -2. Record the selected modifier and reason, separately from character traits.
Predetermined best/worst reaction bounds clamp the resulting category rather than rerolling; a fully predetermined reaction bypasses random generation.

A new approach may permit another reaction unless the initial encounter became a fight. If the audience regards repeated requests as a nuisance, apply cumulative -2 after the first; an authored sufficient wait can reset that penalty.
Eligible influence skills replace the ordinary reaction through the B359 procedure, with applicable reaction modifiers applied to that skill; do not roll both procedures and select the best.
Exact survey measurements require tools, authored time and a surveying check; casually walking an area does not reveal the private exact map. Fast escape prevents simultaneous careful mapping.

An author may allow automatic mapping along obvious landmarks. A reliable map of featureless or precise terrain requires cartography, with default intelligence-5, geography-2, surveying-2 or navigation-4, and direction-sense bonus +3.

Map display scale does not change the one-yard world hex. Area, room and combat display scales are six, two and one hexes per inch; partial boundary hexes count as full hexes for the stated combat-map procedure.
An authored outside rescue gives no bonus character points for escaping that situation; distinguish unrelated session awards from the rescued outcome.

Combat advances by one-second turns, ordinary discussions can consume declared scene time and routine travel can skip uneventful intervals. All modes advance the same game clock and process due effects once.
A session paused mid-adventure does not advance world time merely because real time passes; resuming keeps the same encounter state.

An authored between-adventure interval allocates study, work, healing and long projects through shared time records. Starting an unexpected adventure interrupts affected activities using their own interruption rules.

Optional real-time conversion needs explicit numerator and denominator units. The printed general sentence and following seven-day/seven-week example express inconsistent directions; preserve this ambiguity until a documented policy is chosen.
Session advancement awards are individually authored, commonly zero through five points with two/three average; these are guidelines, not a mandatory automatic amount. Record each award event once.
No session points are awarded when the character's dependent is killed, seriously injured or abducted and unrecovered; integrate the actual dependent event state.
An authored major-story completion award is separate from the session award and may coexist, but cannot be duplicated by repeatedly closing the same milestone.
An advancement award may grant a specified social trait or exercised skill directly instead of discretionary points; update complete accounting without also crediting spendable points.
Job work counts as study at one-quarter time: an eight-hour workday yields two hours study credit. It occupies the same work interval, not eight additional study hours.

Planned, improvised and random encounters create persistent participants and events. An authored cadence and table govern random encounters; advancing a long interval must visit each due boundary once.

A trap requires detection skills/modifiers, safe disabling method, a concrete trigger predicate, and triggered effects including permitted avoidance. Validate all required facts before exposure; puzzle solutions are explicit author actions.

World definitions supply physical conditions, cultures/languages, laws, technology availability and altered/forbidden abilities. Validate a requested operation against its current world rather than the character's birthplace alone.
